observed_mechanics: 0x00b25f40..0x00b25f43 PUSH EBX/EBP/ESI/EDI: four saved registers, no frame pointer established.

0x00b25f44..0x00b25f58 five PUSH immediates, in order 0x018c816a, 0x00b1e500, 0x00b236c0, 0x00d3d420, 0x00b21080. The stack grows down, so the callee reads them as 0x00b21080, 0x00d3d420, 0x00b236c0, 0x00b1e500, 0x018c816a.
0x00b25f5d CALL 0x00b21340, the only direct transfer out of the body. That callee's terminator is c2 14 00 RET 0x14 at 0x00b21407, so it pops all five words itself.
0x00b25f62..0x00b25f6d: EDI = result; ESI = [EDI+0x8] - [EDI+0x4]; EDI += 4; SAR ESI,2. The count is computed once, from an arithmetic shift, so a negative span yields a negative count.
0x00b25f70..0x00b25f74 XOR EBP,EBP / TEST ESI,ESI / JLE: a zero or negative count skips the loop entirely with no probe.

0x00b25f76 MOV EAX,[EDI] is the LOOP HEAD, inside the loop: the container's +0x4 begin word is re-read on every iteration, so a probe that repoints the container mid-walk changes what the next iteration loads.

0x00b25f78..0x00b25f82: EBX = [EAX+EBP*4]; EDX = [EBX] (the candidate's function table); EAX = [EDX+0x4c]; ECX = EBX; CALL EAX. One two-level table load, one indirect transfer, receiver is the candidate, no stack argument is pushed.
0x00b25f84 CMP EAX,[ESP+0x14] compares the full 32-bit probe result against the incoming identity word; no truncation and no sign extension.
0x00b25f88 JZ takes the match path immediately; otherwise INC EBP / CMP EBP,ESI / JL loops back to 0x00b25f76.
The body performs no memory store other than the saved-register pops.

claims.statement: The complete body is 41 instructions spanning 0x00b25f40..0x00b25f9e. objdump and the pack's Ghidra listing agree byte for byte on every instruction and every operand.
ECX is never read and never written by this body. It is therefore not established by this body that a hidden receiver exists; the word is simply forwarded unchanged to 0x00b21340.

One ordinary stack argument at entry_ESP+0x4, callee-cleaned (RET 0x4 on both exits). Both the persisted __thiscall claim and the derived __stdcall claim agree on the cleanup and neither is discriminated further by the listing.
The element count is (end - begin) >> 2 with an arithmetic shift, computed once before the loop from the container's +0x8 and +0x4 words.
The container's +0x4 begin word is re-read on every iteration: the load that yields it is the loop head at 0x00b25f76.
The single indirect transfer dispatches the candidate's function-table word at displacement 0x4c, with ECX holding the candidate and no ordinary stack argument.
The probe's 32-bit result is compared whole against the incoming identity word; the first exact match returns that candidate and stops, and exhaustion returns null.
The body performs no memory store other than the saved-register pops, allocates nothing, and transfers no ownership: the returned candidate is borrowed from the container.
The body pushes the address 0x018c816a and never dereferences it. The data-reference artifact records one row out of this body to that address, in .reloc, access mode 'other'.
A null container is dereferenced at +0x8 and +0x4 with no guard, and a null candidate table or a null 0x4c word reaches the indirect call. No null guard is claimed in either direction.

unresolved_questions: What concrete type is the hidden ECX receiver? The body neither reads nor writes ECX, so this package declares NounProjection as an opaque forwarded word and claims no layout, no owner and no SDK identity for it.

What are the five pushed words 0x00b21080, 0x00d3d420, 0x00b236c0, 0x00b1e500 and the address 0x018c816a? They are code addresses except the last, and nothing in this body says what any of them denotes or how 0x00b21340 uses them.

What class owns the candidate's function table, and what does the method at +0x4c mean? It is called with the candidate as its only argument and returns a raw 32-bit word that this body compares against its caller's word; no name is claimed.

Does the container's +0x4/+0x8 pair belong to a known SDK container, and what is its element type beyond 'a pointer to something with a function table at +0x00'? No capacity, size, allocator or owning-class claim is made, because the body reads neither.

Can the container be mutated between the count being computed and the loop finishing, in a way that makes the frozen count wrong rather than merely re-read? The listing fixes that the count is computed once and the begin word is re-read; whether any caller or the callee does so at runtime is unobserved.

Is the persisted __thiscall claim or the derived __stdcall claim the right SDK identity? Both name callee cleanup and the listing discriminates neither, and the pack records the conflict as unresolved. This package claims only the cleanup.
runtime_gates: The hidden receiver word must be valid for whatever 0x00b21340 does with it; this body does not read it, so nothing here constrains it.
The container returned by 0x00b21340 must have readable +0x04 and +0x08 words and a span whose arithmetic shift by two yields a usable count.
Every candidate reached must have a readable function table whose +0x4c word is a callable probe; the body has no guard on any of these.
The five pushed words and 0x00b21340's own behaviour require original-process observation; nothing about them is established statically here.
The lifetime of a returned candidate is owned by the container and its callees, not by this body, which performs no AddRef, Release, allocation or store.

validation_status.note: ABI FAIL is evidence-side and not a source defect: the evidence pack's derived ABI record carries an unresolved inferred_vs_persisted conflict on calling_convention (__stdcall inferred against __thiscall persisted), and the validator declines to pick a winner between them. Both agree the callee pops the four-byte stack argument, which is the whole of the convention this package claims and all this package declares. FIELDS/OFFSETS is NOT_AVAILABLE because the machine-derived receiver record is present:false with a null base register and an empty offset set -- a correct reflection of this body, which never addresses a receiver. The source therefore declares no member name and reaches its two container words by pinned displacement, so there is no field claim to ground.
